title: MZ Map 1 tile row difference between editor and game

posts.author: 3rr0r1n5ynt4x
posts.body:
Weird situation:
When I create my map in the editor everything seems fine. As soon as I start a game however, my map basically visually moves one row of tiles down and adds an invisible row at the top, which I can move to (outside the screen). The collision detection does not move, so tiles that prevented passing through do not match anymore with the visual layout of the map.
I hope this description is not too confusing.
An example:
You can see the party starting location. Instead of that stop however, the party starts on tile A (directly above, on the fence). The fence can be entered here and moved upon (despite being set to X in the tileset editor). However, I can not enter tile B, here is a collision activated.
Does anyone have an idea what could cause this?
Edit: No active plugins

posts.author: pawsplay
posts.body:
Like, the possibilities are:
- It is unwanted but predictable behavior of something you set
- It is an unwanted and unpredicted behavior, i.e. a bug
- it is a problem with the data on the map
- it is a problem with the data on the map slot
- it is a problem with the data in the tileset
- is is a problem with the game data
- it is a problem with the savegame data
So you're going to have to perform a series of tests that prove or disprove each of those problems. Eg. if the problem does NOT appear on a new map in a new map using the tileset, the problem isn't the game data or the tileset. It would have to be the map, the map slot, or something configured on that map.
Problems with the data or settings could be due to misconfiguration, corruption of the computer data, or a misunderstanding of a function.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
you all forgot a very basic fact: The engine has problems if the map is smaller than the screen.
so
@Accendor
, what is the screen size you set in the system tabs of the database?
have you increased that beyond the original numbers?
because the map shown above is minimum size, and that is not enough when you increase your screen size.

posts.author: 3rr0r1n5ynt4x
posts.body:
Thank you everyone for your feedback and your good ideas on how to best approach testing here. I spend quite some time on it and as it turns out - the problem is not the tileset or the map - it's the character sprite. Turns out it's super misaligned and therefore it just "looks" like it is spawning on the fence, when its actually spawning in the right location. The same is true for collision detection - it's all working as intended it just looks weird because my character is basically hovering in the air.
... that's actually pretty embarrassing, but again thank you everyone for helping me!
